$comment: Closes issue #61: RFC-AITP-0008 §3.1 defines three policy modes (fail_closed, fail_open, soft_fail); before this fixture only fail_closed (rev-001) and soft_fail (rev-002) had a pinned vector, so an implementation could alias fail_open to fail_closed (hard rejection) or treat it as unrecognized and still pass the pack cleanly. Same input as rev-001/rev-002 in every respect but `policy.fail_mode`, so the trio pins all three §3.1 modes against one stale-snapshot shape with exactly one field differing. The snapshot signature placeholder is __VALID_A_SIG__ (issuing peer agentA / kat-keypair-001), signed over the JCS canonical INNER `revocation_list` body, the signature a sibling of the body per RFC-AITP-0008 §1.5. §3.1 distinguishes fail_open ("allow, log a warning") from soft_fail ("allow with restricted grants") only in what the caller is permitted to do next; the wire-level outcome pinned here — success, un-narrowed grants — is identical for both, which this fixture's rationale calls out explicitly since the pack otherwise leaves that distinction unobservable.
description: Same shape as `rev-001`/`rev-002`, but the verifier's policy is `fail_open`: a stale or unreachable snapshot MUST NOT cause hard rejection, and (unlike `soft_fail`) grants MUST NOT be narrowed to a safe subset — the caller gets the request through unmodified. Implementations MAY log a warning. This fixture protects callers that have explicitly opted into availability-first, non-sensitive operation, per §3.1's guidance that fail_open is for read-only, non-sensitive use and MUST NOT be the default for high-value operations. (RFC-AITP-0008 §3.1.)

expected.rationale: fail_open returns `revoked = false` for the queried JTI without narrowing grants, unlike soft_fail. Implementations MAY log a warning flagging the staleness (190000 s vs. policy max of 3600 s), but MUST NOT reject and MUST NOT restrict the request.
